title: Order writes slow down
briefing: Order writes are slower than the service objective. Investigate where write requests spend their time.

actions.label: Inspect write lock waits
actions.criteria: Use when requests acquire database connections promptly but database execution shows lock waits.
actions.instructions: Compare lock wait counters and blocking transactions for order writes.

actions.label: Inspect order writer connection pool
actions.criteria: Use when order write requests spend most of their time acquiring a database connection.
actions.instructions: Compare writer pool utilization and connection acquisition time against query execution time.

actions.label: Compare writer rollout cohorts
actions.criteria: Use when errors align with a writer release and old and new cohorts show different behavior.
actions.instructions: Compare write latency and errors between the previous and current writer versions.

fallback: Collect a trace with acquisition, execution, and response stage timings for one slow write.

events.text: Order write latency p99 exceeds 1.5 seconds. No stage-level timing is attached.
At 02:52 UTC the first trace sample shows acquire=3 ms, execution=1,450 ms, and wait_type=lock on the primary.
The orders trace redaction map uses stage W1 for pool connection acquisition and W2 for database execution. Use the predominant breakdown across a batch over a single trace sample.
New 200-trace batch for slow order writes: 184 traces show W1 over 1,300 ms and W2 below 40 ms. The remaining 16 are mixed.

debrief.summary: The first sampled trace had a real lock wait, but most of the affected requests spent time acquiring a connection from the shared writer pool.
lessons: An early trace can suggest a reasonable diagnostic without representing most failures.
Decode trace stage identifiers and compare timings across a sample.
